name: Build overhead capital work (line crews)
summary: Line crews build the overhead part of the capital program: new pole lines for growth, rebuilds of aging rear-lot and rural lines, and transformer and switch replacements. Once a job is scheduled, the supervisor checks the site, a planner gets buried plant located and switching booked, stores stage the material, and a crew of three journeyperson line technicians and an apprentice builds it with a bucket truck and digger derrick under a work protection permit. The crew lead then hands back redlined drawings and hours for sign-off and the as-built goes to the capital project manager. Most of the elapsed time is waiting: for locates, switching orders, road permits, crew slots and weather, and for back-office sign-off after the work is done.

baseline.org_archetype: A municipally owned Ontario electricity distributor with about 346,000 customers, 2,746 km of overhead line and 20 in-house line crews.
baseline.notes: Describes in-house crew work on jobs released by work scheduling; contractor-built work and emergency restoration are other processes.

trigger: Work scheduling releases the work order to an overhead crew with a planned week (crew schedule).
end_state: The plant is built and energized, crew time is approved and the as-built package has reached the capital project manager; or the job is deferred at the site check.

volume.seasonality: Busiest May to November; frozen ground, snow and short days cut overhead construction from December to March, when crews do more maintenance and trouble work.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate kept: about 1,100 overhead work orders a year fits 20 crews at about 135 available hours a month with roughly half their time on capital work.

surge.cause: autumn push to finish the year's capital program before freeze-up

evidence.note: Common practice for capital programs funded on a calendar year; multiplier is the author's estimate.

Organisation file role and loaded cost (2019-2022 wage x 1.40 for benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead). Eight supervisors cover overhead construction, poles, service work and trouble; about three supervisors' time goes to this process.

systems.name: ERP: general ledger, work orders, purchasing, inventory, fixed assets
Mobile workforce management and field tablets
Document management and engineering drawing repository
Geographic information system (asset and network model)
Ontario One Call member portal and locate management
SCADA for stations and feeder devices
Time entry for crews and staff

resources.name: Overhead line crew (three to four line trades with a bucket truck and a digger)
Light vehicle (pickup or van) for locators, meter technicians, inspectors and field service

steps.name: Review the released job package
steps.description: The overhead lines supervisor opens the scheduled work order in the ERP and mobile workforce tool, reads the design package (drawings, bill of materials, construction standards) and the crew schedule, and assigns a crew lead. They note anything that looks hard to build, such as rear-lot access or heavy framing.

error.defect_description: A design conflict on the drawings is not noticed.

evidence.note: Supervisor review of released jobs; times are the author's estimate for a supervisor running two or three crews.

steps.name: Walk the site with the crew lead
steps.description: The supervisor and crew lead drive to the site, walk the pole line with the drawings, and check truck access, trees, clearances to buildings, existing attachments and soil. They mark changes to pole positions or framing and decide whether the design can be built as drawn.

error.defect_description: An access or clearance problem is missed and found on construction day.

next.condition: job deferred, merged with another job or cancelled

evidence.note: Pre-construction site visits are common practice for line crews; share of jobs with design conflicts is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Revise the design for a field conflict
steps.description: A design technologist opens the drawing in the engineering repository, moves a pole, changes framing or adds an anchor to suit the site, updates the material list in the ERP and reissues the approved drawing to the supervisor.

error.defect_description: Material list not updated to match the revised drawing.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 22/04 ss. 6-7: plans and standard design drawings used in construction must be approved

evidence.note: Approval requirement from ESA guidance; redesign effort and wait are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Submit locate requests
steps.description: The work planner enters each dig location (new pole holes, anchors) on the Ontario One Call portal with the planned dig date and the work order number, and files the ticket numbers on the job.

error.defect_description: Dig area drawn too small or wrong address, so part of the site is not marked.

control.basis: Ontario Underground Infrastructure Notification System Act, 2012 and Occupational Health and Safety Act: locate all buried plant before excavating

steps.name: Wait for underground owners to mark the site
steps.description: The utility's own locators and the gas, telecom, water and municipal owners each mark their buried plant at the site. Owners have five business days to respond to a single-address request; stragglers and re-locates stretch the wait.

error.defect_description: A buried line is marked in the wrong place or missed.

evidence.note: Five business days is about seven calendar days; the spread is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Pick and stage materials
steps.description: A stores attendant prints the material list from the ERP, picks poles from the pole yard and crossarms, insulators, conductor, transformers and hardware from the warehouse, issues them to the work order and stages them on a pole trailer or pallet for the crew.

error.defect_description: Short or wrong item picked, found when the crew unloads on site.

next.condition: item out of stock or on backorder

evidence.note: Picking effort is the author's estimate; staging runs during the locate window, so its wait is short.

steps.name: Chase backordered material
steps.description: The work planner works with the buyer to find a substitute approved item or a delivery date for missing items such as transformers, switches or specific pole classes, and moves the job if the material will not arrive in time.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Transformer and hardware lead times stretched in 2021-2022 supply-chain disruption; share and wait are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Request switching and work protection
steps.description: The work planner sends the control room a switching request with the isolation points, date, crew and protection holder, and asks for planned outage notices when customers will lose power.

error.defect_description: Wrong device or date on the request.

evidence.note: Switching requests go from planners to the control room's switching planners; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Write the switching order
steps.description: A switching and outage planner checks the feeder in the GIS, outage management system and SCADA, writes the step-by-step switching order and grounding points, books the outage window and triggers the customer notices.

error.defect_description: Switching step wrong or an isolation point missed.

control.basis: Utility Work Protection Code (IHSA): work protection permit and tags issued by the control room before work on isolated plant

next.condition: job is off the roadway or on a local street
work in a city road needs a road occupancy permit

evidence.note: Permit and tag system from IHSA; wait and the share of jobs needing a road permit are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the road occupancy permit
steps.description: The City reviews the road occupancy application and traffic control plan for work in the travelled road and issues the permit for set dates. Arterial roads and summer construction season take longer.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Municipal road activity by-law: permit to occupy the road allowance

evidence.note: Road occupancy permits are normal for utility work in city roads; the one to three week wait is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Hold for the booked crew day
steps.description: The job waits for its slot in the crew schedule. The day before, the supervisor confirms the crew, bucket truck and digger derrick, the switching order, the materials and the weather forecast.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: weather, a truck breakdown or emergency work pulls the crew

evidence.note: Line crews are shared with trouble and storm work; postponement share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Reschedule a postponed job
steps.description: The work planner rebooks the crew day, moves the switching order and outage notices with the control room, and tells affected customers of the new date.

error.defect_description: Customers not told of the new outage date.

evidence.note: High winds, lightning, ice and extreme cold stop aerial work; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Drive the crew and trucks to site
steps.description: The crew loads the staged material and drives the bucket truck, digger derrick and pole trailer from the operations centre to the site.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Ottawa service area of 1,116 square kilometres from two operations centres; travel time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Hold the tailboard and set up the work zone
steps.description: The crew lead runs the pre-job briefing and job hazard assessment on the form, sets up traffic control signs and cones, and places the trucks. The crew checks limits of approach and the equipment they will use.

error.defect_description: A hazard is not recorded or discussed.

control.basis: Electrical Utility Safety Rules (IHSA) and Ontario Regulation 213/91: pre-job hazard assessment and traffic protection

next.condition: work on or near energized plant needs isolation
new line not yet energized, or live-line work under hold-off only

evidence.note: Safety rule framework from IHSA; duration and share needing isolation are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Take work protection from the control room
steps.description: The system operator directs the switching; the crew operates field switches and reports each step. The operator issues the work protection permit to the crew's protection holder, who places tags, tests the line dead and applies grounds.

error.defect_description: Device operated out of order.

control.basis: Utility Work Protection Code (IHSA): work protection permit and tags issued by the control room before work on isolated plant

evidence.note: Operator time and the wait for a free console are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Build the overhead plant
steps.description: Three journeyperson line technicians frame and set poles with the digger derrick, install anchors and guys, string and sag conductor from the bucket truck, and hang transformers, switches and arresters to the construction standards. Jobs run from part of a day to several crew days.

error.defect_description: Framing, sag or a connection not to the standard.

evidence.note: Crews of four with a bucket truck and digger are common (source); job length range from the organisation file's one to several days, author's estimate.

steps.name: Work as groundman and assist the build
steps.description: The apprentice works on the ground alongside the journeypersons: rigging material, feeding conductor, digging and tamping, running the derrick controls under supervision and keeping the work zone clear.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Four-person crews with one apprentice follow the organisation file; runs alongside the build.

steps.name: Inspect the completed work
steps.description: A construction inspector checks the work against the construction standards and drawings: clearances, sag, grounding, guying and equipment ratings. They record deficiencies on the inspection form for the crew.

error.defect_description: A deficiency is missed.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 22/04 s. 8: construction inspected and certified safe before it is put into use

evidence.note: The crew lead certifies the remaining jobs; inspection sampling share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Correct deficiencies
steps.description: Two line technicians go back up in the bucket to retension a guy, add a ground or reframe a crossarm as the inspection noted, and tell the inspector it is done.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Release protection and energize
steps.description: The crew removes grounds and tags and the protection holder surrenders the permit. The system operator switches the new or rebuilt section into service and confirms customers are back on.

error.defect_description: Normal configuration not restored in the outage system.

control.basis: Utility Work Protection Code (IHSA): work protection permit and tags issued by the control room before work on isolated plant

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Clean up and return to the yard
steps.description: The crew loads old poles, wire and scrap, tidies the site, drives back, returns unused material to stores against the work order and reports any truck defects.

error.defect_description: Unused material not credited back to the work order.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Complete the work order and redlines
steps.description: The crew lead marks the as-built changes on the drawing, records material used, enters crew hours by work order in the time entry system and completes the job in the mobile tool.

error.defect_description: Redline incomplete or hours charged to the wrong work order.

evidence.note: Paper or tablet redlines were normal in 2019-2022; error rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review and sign off the job
steps.description: The supervisor reviews the crew's hours, the redlines and the hazard assessment, approves the timesheets and signs the job complete. Incomplete redlines or wrong charges go back to the crew lead.

error.defect_description: A wrong charge is approved.

control.basis: Collective agreement and payroll policy: supervisor approval of crew time

next.condition: returned for missing redlines or hours

evidence.note: Return rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Close the field work order and send the as-built
steps.description: The work planner sets the field work order to complete in the ERP, scans the redlined drawings into the document repository and sends the as-built package to the capital project manager for records and capitalisation.

error.defect_description: Scan missing or attached to the wrong job.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Design conflict found at the site check
exceptions.description: The pole position, framing or access does not work as drawn and the design technologist reissues the drawing before locates are requested.

exceptions.name: Backordered material
exceptions.description: A transformer, switch or pole class is not in stock; the planner chases a date or substitute and the job slips.

exceptions.name: Road occupancy permit
exceptions.description: Work in the travelled road waits for the City's permit and traffic plan approval.

exceptions.name: Weather or crew postponement
exceptions.description: Wind, lightning, ice, a truck breakdown or emergency work cancels the crew day and the switching and notices are rebooked.

exceptions.name: Inspection deficiency
exceptions.description: The inspector finds a defect and two technicians go back to fix it before energizing.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from job release to the crew to as-built handed to the project manager
benchmarks.population: Ontario municipal distributor in-house overhead capital jobs, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: two to three weeks of preparation (site check, five-business-day locates, switching order), a crew slot, then one to two weeks of sign-off and close-out. No published figure found.
Line crews of four or five (source); the organisation file uses three to four line trades.
About 25% of all distribution assets past expected life, as reported for the 2026-2030 plan; the organisation file cites 23% of overhead assets.

pain_points.description: Preparation waits (locates, switching order, road permit) add two to three weeks before a crew can start, and a missed locate or permit pushes the crew slot.

evidence.note: Five-business-day locate rule from source; the rest is the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Crews are shared with trouble, storm and service work, so weather or an emergency cancels booked days and all the switching and notices must be rebooked.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common distributor practice.

pain_points.description: Paper or tablet redlines and hours reach the planner days after the work, and incomplete redlines bounce between supervisor and crew lead, delaying as-builts and GIS updates.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; as-built backlogs are a common distributor records problem.

pain_points.description: Material shortages, worst for transformers in 2021-2022, stall staged jobs.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

sources.title: Contractors: locates and safe digging
sources.supports: Locate requests at least five business days before digging (ten for multi-address requests), legally required; hand digging or hydrovac near cables; stay 1.5 m from marked cables; re-locate when marks expire. Current page; the five-business-day rule applied in 2019-2022.

sources.title: Regulation Technical Guidelines (Ontario Regulation 22/04)
sources.supports: Ontario Regulation 22/04: all equipment and plans or standard design drawings must be approved (ss. 6-7); all construction inspected and certified safe before use (s. 8); annual audit of compliance; serious electrical incidents reported to ESA within 48 hours.

sources.title: Keys to the Utility Work Protection Code
sources.publisher: Infrastructure Health and Safety Association (IHSA) Health and Safety Magazine, vol. 23 issue 2
sources.supports: The Electrical Utility Safety Rules govern worker conduct near hazards; the Utility Work Protection Code uses permits and tags to show when lines are safe to work on; issuers and workers must be trained and certified.

sources.title: No two poles are the same
sources.supports: Roadside residential pole replacement 2 to 3 hours, rear-lot or alley 4 to 6 hours, with a line crew of four or five and a bucket truck with auger; steps: clear equipment, remove old pole, dig hole avoiding underground lines, set new pole, reconnect.

sources.title: Wages: Lineworker - Electrical Power Systems in Ontario (NOC 72203)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wage low 29.70, median 49.48, high 62.90; Ottawa region 32.93, 50.63, 63.29 (2024-2025 reference period).

sources.title: Investing in our future: aging infrastructure (2026-2030 investment plan)
sources.supports: About 25% of roughly 165,000 distribution assets have reached end of expected service life; another 15% will within ten years.

assumptions: The process starts when work scheduling releases the job to a crew and ends when the as-built reaches the capital project manager; design, scheduling, locating, switching and GIS posting are separate processes whose hand-offs appear here as steps.

Crew work is recorded as elapsed crew time with people = 3 journeypersons plus a concurrent apprentice step; on travel, tailboard and clean-up steps the apprentice is folded into the three journeypersons, which slightly overstates journeyperson cost and understates apprentice hours.
A multi-day job is one build step whose touch time is the sum of crew working hours; nights between crew days are not added, so simulated elapsed time for multi-day jobs is a little short.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (wage x 1.40).
About 65% of jobs need isolation and a work protection permit; the rest are new, not yet energized lines or live-line work under a reclose hold-off.

The simulated median (about 36 days) sits slightly above the 30-day benchmark estimate because preparation waits are added in sequence; in practice a planner sometimes requests locates and switching in parallel, which shortens the elapsed time by a few days.
Wait times describe 2019-2022 practice, including pandemic-era supply delays for transformers in 2021-2022.
